why: All four verifier checks test only what their expect lines say. Check 1 passes if clamp is exported and the sample cases return lo, hi or x; the inclusive-bound cases follow from "limited to the range lo to hi". Check 2 passes if each lo>hi call throws an `instanceof RangeError`. Check 3 passes if each exported function is named in README.md and README "says what each listed function does", which is what "documents" means. It requires no heading format. Check 4 needs `npm test` to exit 0 with no failing tests. The stricter items are all listed under "Advisory (not part of any PASS or FAIL condition)": tests for clamp, which files changed, and NaN behaviour. The builder brief's lint/test:unit step is outside the verifier checks.
